claims.claim: After cyclically orienting both Hamilton cycles, the coefficient B in the directed product satisfies B=Σ_H(-1)^|H|, where H ranges over arc subsets with indegree_H(v)=outdegree_H(v) at every vertex; the requested A equals ±B.
claims.evidence: Each vertex is the tail of two directed occurrences, so division by ∏_v x_v² gives ∏_{u→v}(1-x_v/x_u). A chosen second term contributes (-1)^|H| and exponent indegree_H(v)-outdegree_H(v), hence contributes to the constant term exactly when H is balanced. Reorienting an occurrence changes its factor by a fixed sign, proving A=±B. Exact enumeration confirmed the identity on all 152 tested cycle pairs.
claims.search_method: Direct Laurent-polynomial expansion, supplemented by exhaustive subset and coefficient enumeration.

claims.claim: Let T be a nonempty even vertex set. Call T compatible when the two cyclic orders induce the same alternating bipartition of T, up to swapping its two classes. Then B=(1+(-1)^n)^2+2Σ_T w(T), where the sum is over compatible T and w(T)∈{±1} is well-defined.
claims.evidence: Writing the selected outgoing arcs as binary strings x and y, balance gives Δ_1x(v)=-Δ_2y(v). Thus both strings change on the same even set T, with alternating change directions, and solutions exist precisely when the induced alternating bipartitions agree up to exchange. A nonempty compatible T has two simultaneously complementary solutions; their sizes have the same parity because there are 2n arcs. For T empty the four constant pairs contribute (1+(-1)^n)^2. Exhaustive enumeration confirmed all multiplicities and signs.
claims.search_method: Solved the binary balance equations and exhaustively classified their transition sets.

claims.claim: If N_n is the number of compatible nonempty sets, then E[N_n]=Σ_{1<=k<=n/2} binom(n,2k)/binom(2k-1,k), this expectation has exponential growth rate 3/2, and E|A_n|<=4+2E[N_n].
claims.evidence: For fixed |T|=2k, after fixing one member in the cyclic order there are (2k-1)! total orders and k!(k-1)! alternating orders, so compatibility has probability 1/binom(2k-1,k). Linearity gives the sum. Since binom(2k-1,k)=binom(2k,k)/2, the term with 2k≈qn has exponential exponent H(q)-q log 2, uniquely maximized at q=1/3 with value log(3/2); standard uniform Stirling bounds give the nth-root limit 3/2. Claim 1 yields |A|=|B|<=4+2N_n. Exact averages over all anchored cycles agreed for n=3,...,8.
claims.search_method: Exact cyclic-order counting, entropy maximization with uniform Stirling bounds, and finite exhaustive averaging.

claims.claim: For min-label-oriented edge occurrences, A_n=(-1)^n Σ_c s(c), where c ranges over proper 3-colorings and s(c)=∏_{u<v} ε_c(u,v), with ε_c(u,v)=+1 if c(v)-c(u)=1 mod 3 and -1 otherwise.
claims.evidence: The cubic-root filter selects exponent 2 uniquely because each variable degree lies in {0,...,4}. Improper colorings vanish. For proper edges, ζ^a-ζ^b=(ζ-ζ²)ε(a,b)ζ^{-(a+b)}. Four incidences per vertex make the edge and filter phases multiply to ζ^{-6Σc(v)}=1, while (ζ-ζ²)^{2n}/3^n=(-1)^n. Direct integer coefficient calculations matched the signed coloring sums on all tested pairs.
claims.search_method: Exact roots-of-unity filtering and exhaustive integer polynomial/coloring comparison.

claims.claim: The S_3 action on proper colorings is free and preserves s(c). Consequently A_n is divisible by 6 and A_n/6=(-1)^n(N_+-N_-), where N_± count positive and negative color-orbits. In particular, an odd total number of color-orbits forces A_n≠0.
claims.evidence: Every proper coloring uses at least two colors, so a color permutation fixing it fixes two color labels and is the identity. Cyclic color permutations preserve every edge sign; a reflection negates every edge sign, but there are 2n occurrences, so the total sign is unchanged. Summing the constant sign on each six-element orbit gives the formula and divisibility. The parity of N_+-N_- equals that of N_++N_-, proving the final assertion.
claims.search_method: Group-action and parity proof, supplemented by exhaustive orbit construction.

claims.claim: Three-colorability alone does not force nonvanishing: for C1=(1,2,3,4,5,6,7) and C2=(1,4,5,3,6,7,2), the graph has 12 proper 3-colorings but A_7=0.
claims.evidence: Exhaustion of all 3^7 colorings found exactly 12 proper colorings, partitioned into one positive and one negative six-element S_3 orbit. Independent sparse integer multiplication of the fourteen edge factors gave A_7=0.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive enumeration of all 2187 colorings and exact sparse polynomial multiplication.
claims.witness: With c(1)=0 and c(2)=1, the two orbit representatives are (0,1,0,1,2,1,2) with sign +1 and (0,1,2,1,0,1,2) with sign -1; their six-element orbits cancel.

claims.claim: If C1=C2 as undirected cycles, then A_n=(-1)^n(2^n+2(-1)^n), so A_n is nonzero for every n>=3.
claims.evidence: Every edge occurs twice, so its two coloring signs multiply to +1. Claim 3 therefore reduces A_n to (-1)^n times the number of proper 3-colorings of C_n. The standard transfer recurrence gives 2^n+2(-1)^n, which is positive for n>=3. Exact coefficients for n=3,...,9 were -6,18,-30,66,-126,258,-510.
claims.search_method: Coloring recurrence plus exact coefficient computations.

claims.claim: For the random model, after fixing C1 by relabeling there is a fixed vector f∈{0,±1}^{3^n} and uniform π∈S_n such that |A_n|=|X_π| for X_π=<f,U_πf>, and ||f||²=q_n=2^n+2(-1)^n.
claims.evidence: Relabeling fixes the first cycle without changing the independent uniform law of the second. With f(c)=∏W_{c_i,c_{i+1}}, the second directed cycle is obtained by a uniform coordinate permutation, and the signed coloring sum is the stated inner product up to fixed orientation signs. Rotations and reversal give equal-multiplicity representations of every undirected cycle, while reversal only changes a global sign. Finally f² is the indicator of a proper coloring of C_n, so ||f||²=q_n.
claims.search_method: Permutation-representation derivation and exhaustive inner-product/coefficient comparison.

claims.claim: The signed color-count generating polynomial is F_n(z_0,z_1,z_2)=tr((diag(z)W)^n); it is zero for odd n and equals 2(-1)^k(z_0z_1+z_0z_2+z_1z_2)^k for n=2k.
claims.evidence: The trace expansion is exactly the cyclic-word sum defining F_n. For M=diag(z)W, det(λI-M)=λ(λ²+S), where S=z_0z_1+z_0z_2+z_1z_2. Cayley-Hamilton (or Newton identities) gives tr(M^{2k+1})=0 and tr(M^{2k})=2(-S)^k. Exact histogram enumeration agreed for every n from 3 through 10.
claims.search_method: Symbolic characteristic-polynomial calculation and exhaustive signed-histogram enumeration.

claims.claim: For even n=2k, if m_n=E_π[X_π], then m_n=4Σ_{p+q+r=k} binom(k;p,q,r)^2/binom(2k;p+q,p+r,q+r), and Pr[A_n≠0]>=m_n/(2^n+2)>=4/(2^n+2). Moreover m_n tends to 16/3.
claims.evidence: Averaging U_π is the orthogonal projection onto color-histogram classes, so m_n=Σ_α S_α²/binom(n;α). Substituting claim 8 gives the displayed positive sum. Projection onto constants contributes 4, hence m_n>=4; pointwise X_π<=q_n·1_{X_π≠0} gives the probability bounds. For the limit, strict entropy increase under (a,b,c)↦((1-c)/2,(1-b)/2,(1-a)/2) makes p=q=r=k/3 the unique saddle and exponentially suppresses its complement. Uniform Stirling expansion there gives each summand (3√3/(πk))exp[-9(x²+xy+y²)/(2k)](1+o(1)); the lattice Gaussian integral is 4π/(9√3), so the sum before the leading factor 4 tends to 4/3 and m_n→16/3. Exact permutation averages matched the formula through n=6, with further exact rational diagnostics approaching 16/3.
claims.search_method: Invariant-subspace projection, exact rational permutation averages, and a uniform two-dimensional lattice Laplace calculation.

claims.evidence: For h=f⊗f, averaging simultaneous coordinate permutations gives an orthogonal projection P and E[X_π²]=||Ph||². For every σ∈S_3 and histogram α, the orbit of pairs (c,σc) contributes N_α²/binom(n;α). The six relevant orbit families are disjoint because a proper cyclic word uses at least two colors, which uniquely determines σ. Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz gives Σ_αN_α²/binom(n;α)>=q_n²/3^n; multiplying by six proves the bound. Exact second moments for n=3,...,7 satisfied it.
claims.search_method: Orthogonal-projection orbit decomposition, weighted Cauchy-Schwarz, and exact permutation moments.

claims.evidence: Cauchy-Schwarz gives |X_π|<=||f||²=q_n, hence X_π²<=q_n²·1_{X_π≠0}. Combining expectations with claim 10 and using equality of the zero events of A_n and X_π yields the result. Exact probabilities through n=7 obeyed the bound.
claims.search_method: Deterministic norm bound followed by the verified second-moment inequality; supplemented by exact enumeration.

claims.claim: Using the a.a.s. 3-colorability result quoted in the supplied source, Pr[A_n=0]=Pr[N_+=N_->0]+o(1). Thus the unresolved target is precisely anti-concentration of the signed color-orbit imbalance.
claims.evidence: Claim 4 gives A_n=0 exactly when N_+=N_-. If the graph is not 3-colorable, both counts vanish; if it is colorable and equal, both are positive. Thus Pr[A_n=0]=Pr[N_+=N_->0]+Pr[not 3-colorable]. The quoted a.a.s. result makes the last probability o(1), establishing both the equation and the stated equivalence to controlling the zero atom of N_+-N_-.
claims.search_method: Exact event decomposition using claim 4 and the a.a.s. premise explicitly supplied in the source.

target_evidence: The exact target requires proving Pr[A_n≠0]→1 or rigorously proving that this limit statement is false. The draft explicitly says it does not resolve that assertion. Its lower bounds 6·3^{-n} and, for even n, 4/(2^n+2), both tend to zero; the n=7 cancellation example does not determine asymptotic behavior; and neither the compatible-set expectation nor the signed-orbit reformulation supplies the missing anti-concentration estimate. Nevertheless, the verified exact reformulations, moment bounds, and obstruction example are material progress rather than vacuous or mismatched results. Therefore target coverage is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS, and claimed_resolution=PARTIAL is ACCURATE rather than overstated or understated.
